title: Emerald Savings - Federated VPC sizing, upgrade & rollback playbook (draft)
content:
Context and purpose:

This is an engineering-facing draft specifically tailored for Emerald Savings to validate a federated VPC private deployment of Redwood Private. It combines: 1) initial capacity sizing, 2) Terraform module and variable recommendations, 3) upgrade and rollback choreography, and 4) an architecture Q&A log with assumptions for security and regulatory constraints.

High-level deployment summary:
- Deployment model: Federated VPC peering model connecting Emerald Savings' primary AWS account (prod account A) and a secondary DR account (account B). Redwood control plane will be customer-hosted in the primary account (customer-managed control plane mode).
- Target footprint (Phase 1): 2 production inference clusters (ssd-mounted), 1 staging cluster, 1 set of batch workers for nightly embeddings.
- Hardware baseline: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent (per prod cluster) NVMe-backed nodes for fast KV cache; staging uses 2 x A100-80GB. Batch workers use 8 x T4-equivalent for throughput jobs.

Sizing assumptions and numbers (rationale included):
- Expected peak QPS: 350 rps across two prod clusters (sustained peaks up to 550 rps during business hours). We assume 50 tokens per request average.
- Token/sec capacity per A100 node (conservative): 40k tokens/sec. With 4 nodes per prod cluster -> ~160k tokens/sec per cluster. This provides headroom for bursts and background tasks.
- Memory/KV cache sizing: 160GB of KV-resident memory per node recommended (use instance families with ≥512GB system RAM if using model sharding).
- Storage: Local NVMe 4TB per node for model shards + shard checkpointing; S3-compatible object store for artifacts and model backups.
- Network: 25 Gbps minimum NIC per node; recommend 100 Gbps connectivity inside the VPC fabric if available for inter-node NN communication when sharded.
- Capacity for embeddings batch: nightly jobs estimated to process 12M documents/month -> use 8 T4s with autoscaling window to handle backfill.

Terraform module notes and variable recommendations:
- Use the private-deployments/rds-kms-terraform module (branch: emerald-customizations) with these input variables:
  - instance_count_prod_cluster = "4"
  - instance_type_prod = "p4d.24xlarge" (or equivalent A100-80GB family)
  - enable_nvme = "true"
  - kms_key_alias = "alias/emerald-rw-private"
  - s3_endpoint = "s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"
  - enable_control_plane_private_endpoint = "true"
  - mgmt_subnet_ids = ["subnet-xxxx","subnet-yyyy"] (populated from customer infra)
- Module changes suggested (PR to create):
  1) Add variable allow_listed_peers (CIDR and account IDs) to make peering explicit in the module instead of separate tf script.
  2) Add toggle for HSM-backed KMS integration (hsm_kms_enabled bool) to conditionally create custom grants.
  3) Introduce lifecycle rule for local NVMe-backed snapshots to prevent accidental deletion during upgrades: create snapshot before drain.

Upgrade plan (minor version + quantized runtime update):
- Window and prerequisites:
  - Target window: 02:00–05:00 local time (low traffic), with a secondary window 14:00–16:00 if rollback required.
  - Ensure model registry snapshot exists on S3 and Terraform plan has been applied in staging.
  - Verify KMS grants and HSM attestation are current; confirm cross-account grants for DR account.
- Steps (canary-first):
  1) Create infra snapshot (NVMe checkpoint + model registry snapshot).
  2) Apply Terraform in staging cluster: update runtime image tag, enable quantized kernels behind feature flag. Smoke test on staging.
  3) Canary rollout on prod cluster A: pick 1 node, cordon, drain, deploy new runtime, restart agent, run deterministic eval prompt set (top-3 prompts from eval harness).
  4) Monitor latency P95/P99, error rates and KL divergence on outputs for 30 minutes.
  5) If metrics stable, proceed rolling update across remaining nodes in that cluster. Pause between nodes for 10 minutes to validate.
  6) Repeat process for prod cluster B.
  7) Post-upgrade: run full regression eval suite and cost-per-token snapshot.

Rollback plan (fast fallback):
- Trigger: sustained P99 latency > 2x baseline or failed regressions (quality delta above agreed thresholds).
- Quick rollback steps:
  1) Revert runtime image tag via Terraform variable and apply to node(s) failing.
  2) If nodes are unresponsive, spin up instances from pre-upgrade snapshot AMI in the same AZ and rejoin cluster using the previous model registry snapshot.
  3) Re-enable traffic to stable cluster and isolate degraded cluster behind routing rule (weight 0).
  4) Post-rollback: create incident ticket, collect logs, and schedule root cause follow-up.

Networking, security and compliance assumptions (customer-specific):
- Emerald requires all traffic between Redwood runtime and customer services to traverse VPC endpoints; no public egress for inference traffic is permitted.
- KMS: keys must be customer-owned, HSM-backed (FIPS-140-2 Level 3 preferred). Team has requested that we include an HSM-ready toggle in the Terraform module.
- Audit: all inference requests must be logged to CloudWatch/Panoply with immutable retention for 7 years. We will instrument request IDs at the load-balancer and application layer.
- Private subnets: Control plane endpoints will be placed in private subnets with NAT-only egress for patching windows.

Operational runbook (short checklists):
- Day 0 (initial deploy):
  - Validate terraform plan with emerald infra team in shared workspace.
  - Confirm KMS grants and customer IAM roles are correctly bound.
  - Deploy prod cluster A (scale 1 node), smoke test, then scale to full node count.
  - Configure VPC routing and peering acceptance.
- Daily ops (first 30 days):
  - Monitor token/sec, KV cache hit rates, disk utilization, and p95 latency.
  - Checkpoint snapshots nightly and verify next-day restore on staging weekly.
- Incident triage:
  - Collect /var/log/redwood/agent.log, kernel-level NIC stats, and terraform state diff.
  - If degraded model quality, run eval harness to determine delta.

Open questions for Emerald engineering (to confirm before finalizing TF code):
1) Which NIC family is guaranteed across datacenter zones? Do we have 100 Gbps fabrics in all three AZs?
2) Confirm HSM vendor and whether the customer requires on-prem PKCS#11 bridge or cloud HSM.
3) Are there regulatory requirements for model artifacts to remain in-country? If yes, confirm object store region constraints.
4) Preferred maintenance window and blackout dates for patching.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: NVMe snapshot corruption during high IOPS snapshot. Mitigation: use filesystem freeze + application-level checkpoint and incremental snapshots; test snapshot restore during staging weekly.
- Risk: Terraform drift causing security group expansion. Mitigation: enable policy-as-code guardrails (OPA) and run pre-commit checks; require peer approval for security group tf changes.
- Risk: HSM integration delays. Mitigation: design module to accept both HSM-backed KMS and customer-managed KMS secrets so work can proceed in parallel.

Next steps and owner map:
- Action: Confirm NIC families and HSM vendor (owner: Emerald infra lead) - due EOD 2025-11-10.
- Action: Redwood eng to open PR for module toggles (owner: Arjun Patel) - due 2025-11-14.
- Action: Run full restore drill in staging (owner: Maya Chen / SRE) - due prior to production cutover.

Appendix: quick Terraform snippet (illustrative)

module "emerald_prod_cluster" {
  source = "git::github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-cluster.git//modules/cluster?ref=emerald-customizations"
  cluster_name = "emerald-prod-a"
  instance_count = 4
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  nvme_enabled = true
  kms_key_alias = "alias/emerald-rw-private"
  allowed_peer_accounts = ["111122223333"]
}

Notes: this snippet is intentionally minimal; full variable files will be maintained in the customer repo under emerald-infra/terraform/prod.tfvars.

---
If this draft looks reasonable, I will: a) convert module suggestions into a PR with tests, b) run a constrained capacity simulation on staging to validate KV cache settings, and c) produce a one-page architecture diagram for the Emerald security review.

Feedback requested: confirm HSM approach (cloud HSM vs on-prem bridge), NIC bandwidth guarantees, and the DST maintenance blackout dates so we can lock the upgrade windows.
